oewn-01934070-v.learner: to travel in a vehicle, or to be carried somewhere in one
examples: Elizabeth, as they drove along, watched for the first appearance of Pemberley Woods
They descended the hill, crossed the bridge, and drove to the door

oewn-01508789-v.learner: to make someone or something move back, by force or by influence
examples: I wonder who first discovered the efficacy of poetry in driving away love!
it is not for me to be driven away by Mr. Darcy

oewn-01934845-v.learner: to work the controls of a vehicle and make it go where you want
examples: He learned to drive a car when he was seventeen.

oewn-10373054-n.learner: the son of your brother or of your sister
examples: Has he, has my nephew, made you an offer of marriage?
My daughter and my nephew are formed for each other.

oewn-00609334-v.learner: to bring back into your mind something you knew before; to have a memory of it
examples: if I recollect right, he went but the day before
However, I recollected afterwards, that if he had been prevented going, the wedding need not be put off

oewn-08005299-n.learner: two people who live together as a pair
examples: Her parents were an odd match, but they lived happily together for forty years.

oewn-09920434-n.learner: a person who is seen as a good person to marry
examples: With his fortune and his easy manners, he was thought an excellent match for any young lady.

connotation.why: sizes a person up as a prize to be won in marriage

oewn-03733928-n.learner: a thin stick of wood or card with a tip that catches fire when you rub it on something
examples: He took a match from the box and struck it against the side.

oewn-02024442-v.learner: to get to the place or point you were going to, whether it is a real place or not
examples: within four hours of their leaving Hunsford they reached Mr. Gardiner's house
They travelled as expeditiously as possible; and sleeping one night on the road, reached Longbourn by dinnertime the next day.

oewn-02010848-v.learner: to come to a certain time, or to a certain state or level
examples: which would have injured a higher degree of excellence than she had reached

oewn-01442758-v.learner: to move your hand or body forward or upward so that you can touch something; this can also be meant in a figurative way
examples: She reached across the table for the salt.

oewn-02631867-v.learner: to start to be there, or to come up

Were the same fair prospect to arise at present, as had flattered them a year ago

oewn-00340548-v.learner: to happen as a result of something else
examples: he was fond of the country and of books; and from these tastes had arisen his principal enjoyments
feelings which arise only from a half hour's acquaintance

oewn-02630344-v.learner: to begin to exist, or to take on a form or a shape

oewn-06314878-n.learner: a word or phrase used for one particular thing
examples: we must not use the term miniature in its restricted sense
And though he exclaimed at the term, she found that it had been pretty much the case.

oewn-06783666-n.learner: a statement of what is required as part of an agreement; the word is usually plural
examples: There was just such an informality in the terms of the bequest as to give me no hope from law.
but the terms, I suppose, must be complied with

oewn-15249282-n.learner: a period of time that has a fixed length

oewn-04989190-n.learner: the particular sound, pitch, or state of the way a person speaks
examples: "I am," said he, with a firm voice.
At length, in a voice of forced calmness, he said

oewn-07125323-n.learner: the sound made when the folds in your throat shake, shaped by the passage above them

oewn-00833312-v.learner: to tell someone about a fact, a situation, or an event

oewn-00523693-v.learner: to give something its character or its basic nature

oewn-00834860-v.learner: to act as someone who tells the police or those in power about another person

oewn-00579810-v.learner: to make someone or something seem attractive or acceptable
examples: They have none of them much to recommend them

oewn-00876672-v.learner: to press for something to be done
examples: convinced that no country advice could be of any service, recommended an express to town for one of the most eminent physicians

oewn-00884469-v.learner: to say that you think well of someone or something
examples: Her old teacher recommended her warmly to the new employer.
